statement: Let G be the undirected graph with vertex set {0,1,...,len(strs)-1} in which two distinct vertices i and j are adjacent exactly when strs[i] and strs[j] are similar, where two strings x and y of equal length are similar iff x = y or there exist distinct positions p and q with 0 <= p < q < len(x), x[p] = y[q], x[q] = y[p], and x[k] = y[k] for every k with 0 <= k < len(x) and k not in {p,q}. Then the function returns a result r equal to the number of connected components of G; equivalently, r is the number of equivalence classes of the reflexive-transitive closure of the edge relation on the index set, i.e., the relation in which i and j are equivalent iff i = j or there is a finite path of edges from i to j.
preconditions: 1 <= len(strs) <= 300; there exists an integer L with 1 <= L <= 300 such that len(strs[i]) = L for every i with 0 <= i < len(strs); every byte of every strs[i] is a lowercase ASCII letter (97 <= byte <= 122); and for every i,j with 0 <= i < len(strs) and 0 <= j < len(strs), strs[i] and strs[j] are anagrams, i.e., for every byte value c the number of positions k with strs[i][k] = c equals the number of positions k with strs[j][k] = c.

statement: The function returns a result r; in particular, it does not panic, does not access an out-of-bounds index, and does not overflow 64-bit signed integer arithmetic.

statement: Let S be the set of distinct byte-vectors occurring among strs[0],...,strs[len(strs)-1]. Form the undirected graph H on S where two distinct values x and y are adjacent exactly when x and y are similar (x = y, or there exist distinct positions p<q with x[p]=y[q], x[q]=y[p], and x[k]=y[k] for all k not in {p,q}). Then r equals the number of connected components of H.
